rule: Derek 2026-10-14 (#6694): a page either auditor calls worse is not written; STOP if Opus calls any worse or Gemini > 4/40

worse.line: B worse (yes/no) (nominal): α −0.04 [−0.09, 0.00], 40 pages — not settled

rows.opus_note: X garbles the text throughout (e.g. 'Kindligkeit ein bund alles lieb aber da wollen' for 'findligkeit ein, und soll sich aber der Leser') and gives page-num 30 where the leaf shows '3'.
rows.gemini_note: X severely misreads the text throughout, rendering 'Vatter und Sohn' as 'wetter kund Rofe' and 'ungrundes' as 'begindes'.

rows.opus_note: The print reads 'ἀπίει', 'ὀγκοῦτο' and 'τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ' as X has them; Y normalizes these to 'ἀπῄει', 'ὠγκοῦτο', 'τὰ γὰρ'.
rows.gemini_note: X faithfully transcribes the printed readings such as 'ὀγκοῦτο' and 'τὸ γὰρ', whereas Y alters them to 'ὠγκοῦτο' and 'τὰ γὰρ'.

rows.opus_note: Same text in both; X keeps the abbreviations ('differūt', 'cōueniunt') and Y expands them, which is a convention difference.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads the page number '11.' as 'II.' and alters 'rimat.' to 'rimatur.'.

rows.opus_note: X has 'causa omnium mutuum naturalium' where the print reads 'motuum'; Y is correct and also keeps the 'cœli' spelling.
rows.gemini_note: X introduces a sense-changing error by transcribing 'motuum' as 'mutuum' in 'causa omnium motuum naturalium'.

rows.opus_note: X drops abbreviation marks and gets forms wrong ('Xathippi cynotaphiu', 'boue', 'inspergeda', 'sub uite') where the print has 'Xāthippi cynotaphiū', 'bouē', 'inspergēda'; Y renders them correctly.
rows.gemini_note: Y correctly transcribes the text, whereas X leaves abbreviations unexpanded resulting in errors like 'Xathippi' and erroneously splits 'abstine re'.

rows.opus_note: Y misreads 'amplexandam' as 'amplectendam', 'Quā … nauarit' as 'Quae … nauit' and 'inserat' as 'inferat'; X follows the print.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'disserendi' as 'differendi' and alters 'Quam ... nauarit' to 'Quae ... nauit'.

rows.opus_note: The print reads 'ea ocia' and 'Billij', as in Y; X has 'otia' and 'Billy' (minor).
rows.gemini_note: Both transcriptions are equally faithful, as the minor spelling variations between 'otia' and 'Billy' in X versus 'ocia' and 'Billij' in Y do not matter to a reader.

rows.opus_note: Y adds a whole commentary paragraph ('Es ist hier zu mercken / daß der Herr des Weinbergs…') that does not appear on this leaf.
rows.gemini_note: Y invents an entire second column of commentary ('Es ist hier zu mercken / daß der Herr des Weinbergs') not present on the leaf.

rows.opus_note: Almost identical; Y has 'comeset' where the print reads 'comeßet' (X: 'comesset'), and Y adds the catchword 'ipsas' to the text.
rows.gemini_note: X is more faithful because Y erroneously appends the catchword 'ipsas' to the body text and leaves an extraneous semicolon in 'occultumque;'.

rows.opus_note: The print reads 'Untzen', 'eintzelich', 'weisse' and 'Gieß-Puckel', as in X; Y modernizes these to 'Unzen', 'einzelich', 'weiße', 'Gieß-Buckel'.
rows.gemini_note: X accurately preserves the original printed spellings 'Untzen', 'eintzelich', and 'Gieß-Puckel', whereas Y regularizes them to 'Unzen', 'einzelich', and 'Gieß-Buckel'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf reads 'Expauit famam' (as X has it); Y's 'Expuit famam' changes 'took fright at' to 'spat out'. Otherwise the texts are identical, and both record the catchword 'Felices tenebrae'.
rows.gemini_note: X reads 'Expauit' where the leaf has 'Expuit' in line 13.

rows.opus_note: The texts match apart from long-s conventions. Y misreads 'sed altero' as 'sed aftero' and invents a 'classical scene' for the woodcut initial, which actually shows two small figures, as X says.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'altero' as 'afte-ro' at the line break and splits 'uires' into 'ui res' in the margin.

rows.opus_note: Y drops 'ἔρον' ('ἀναπαύσιος ἔρον ἔχει'), garbles many Greek words ('ζέπηται', 'ῥέοις', 'λουζὰ', 'σεμνὰ ... ῥαχεία' for 'τρέπηται', 'νέοις', 'λουτρὰ', 'στρωμνὰ ... τραχεῖα') and has 'fit' for 'sit' in the Latin.
rows.gemini_note: Y severely corrupts the Greek column with misreadings such as 'σεμνὰ δὲ οὐ ῥαχεία' for 'στρωμνὰ δὲ οὐ τραχεῖα' and dropping 'ρον' from 'ἔρον ἔχει'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf has page number '3292' and 'Pag. 554'; X gives '1202' and '854'. X also turns the Florentine reading 'extraneasse' and the phrase 'extraneus heres' into 'externasse' and 'externare heras'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'extraneus heres' as 'externare heras' and 'Alluximus' as 'Altissimus'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf has the καί ligature in 'λιμέσιν καὶ' and 'Δὴ τότε καὶ', which X renders as 'ἢ'. X also drops 'καὶ' in note 123, gives 'infano' for 'insano', puts Arabic letters into the Hebrew, and adds a spurious sig '126'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'ἄλλυδις ἄλλο' as 'ἄλλυσις ἄλο', misreads 'καὶ' as 'ἢ' multiple times, and inserts Arabic characters into the Hebrew quotation ('וبلشون').

rows.opus_note: Y omits 'l' in 'semiperipheria l f d' and writes 'anguli a d deinceps ... angulis a d deinceps' where the leaf has 'ad u' and 'ad o'. It also has 'ex hypothesi' for 'ex thesi' and 'per 12 p 1' for 'per 13 p 1'.
rows.gemini_note: Y corrupts geometric points and citations, reading 'anguli a d deinceps' for 'anguli ad u' and '[per 12 p 1]' for '[per 13 p 1]'.

rows.opus_note: The main text is the same, apart from X's systematic 'f' for long s ('ficco', 'effentia'). The right-hand marginal notes are cut off and survive only as fragments ('A ta re ri', 'So Ge tu cu mi'); Y marks them unclear, while X invents full notes such as 'Acre', 'Solutio.' and 'Generatio & interitus.'
rows.gemini_note: Y omits the column section letters and legible marginal notes such as 'Solutio.' and 'Generatio & interitus.', incorrectly treating them as cut-off fragments.

rows.opus_note: The right edge of the text is cut off. Y marks the lost endings with '[...]'; X silently fills them in ('Er-/fahrung', 'Na-/hrung' where the leaf shows 'Erf...' / 'rung'). X also normalises 'niemahls' and 'Schwantz'.
rows.gemini_note: Y accurately marks the cropped right edge with [...], whereas X invents text not on the leaf by transcribing 'Er-' and 'fahrung' instead of 'Erf' and 'rung', and line 5 'haben' instead of 'ben'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf's gloss reads '妻去聲下同縲力追反絏息列反', as Y has it. X replaces the fanqie readings with an invented '縲音雷絏音屑'.
rows.gemini_note: X replaces the printed fanqie glosses ('縲力追反絏息列反') with invented readings ('縲音雷絏音屑').

rows.opus_note: Y turns 'Clā uiro' (Clam uiro) into a new speaker line 'Cl. a uiro'. It also misreads 'Neq; salsum' as 'falsum', 'inijcio' as 'inuicio' and 'sanun es' as 'sanus es'.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'Clā uiro' as an invented speaker turn 'Cl. a uiro' and transcribes 'inijcio' as 'inuicio'.

rows.opus_note: X is badly garbled and misreads the leaf (e.g. 'rex signa orit[ur]' for 'sex signa oriuntur', '20000' for '252000', 'Duo aute[m] circuli' for 'Horum autem circulorum'), whereas Y follows the hand closely.
rows.gemini_note: X garbles multiple passages into nonsensical text (e.g., 'Item gognes anecho' for 'Item quicquid a medio mouetur') and misreads key numbers like 700 as '500'.

rows.opus_note: Y matches the print with 'quorunque' and 'quoniam et in ea legitur'; X has 'quorumque' and drops the 'et'.
rows.gemini_note: Y accurately preserves the printed spelling 'quorunque' and includes 'et' in 'quoniam et in ea legitur', which X omits.

rows.opus_note: X misreads 'inania utilibus' as 'immania', a change of sense, and also has 'aspernerentur' and 'nobiliaribus' where the print reads 'aspernarentur' and 'nobilioribus'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'inania utilibus' as 'immania utilibus' and 'nobilioribus' as 'nobiliaribus'.

rows.opus_note: The body text is identical apart from long-s use; the only other difference is the header ('Oraculis.' vs the printed 'Oraculu.').
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads the running header 'Oraculis.' as 'Oraculu.'.

rows.opus_note: X drops the line 'So war ein Christ gebilt nach CHRISTI Wort und Leben/' and garbles the next one as 'So saher Christlich aus'.
rows.gemini_note: X omits the line 'So war ein Christ gebilt nach CHRISTI Wort und Leben/'.

rows.opus_note: X correctly reads 'relicturo' and the Greek 'ἄρθρα σὺν ἄρθροις', where Y has 'relicto' and 'ἄνδρα σὺν ἀνδρείοις'; X's only slip is 'εὐνούχισαν' for the printed 'εὐνουχίσθησαν'.
rows.gemini_note: Y corrupts 'ἄρθρα σὺν ἄρθροις ἔχων' into 'ἄνδρα σὺν ἀνδρείοις ἔχων' and misreads 'relicturo' as 'relicto'.

rows.opus_note: X keeps the printed 'angenohmen' and 'Dispositon' and gets the dashes right ('— —, —, und —'); Y normalises the spelling and adds an extra dash plus a superscript 'a'.
rows.gemini_note: Y omits the number '5' ('also 5 recht gut dabey versorgt worden') and normalizes 'angenohmen' to 'angenommen'.

rows.opus_note: X garbles many entries (e.g. 'Balatus.us.ui.o damo ꝓui' for 'dicitur clamor ouium') and leaves out the printed 'a balea baleos vel balerica vel balearis'; Y expands the abbreviations faithfully.
rows.gemini_note: X omits '⁊ a balea baleos vel balerica vel balearis' and garbles 'clamor ouiū' as 'o damo ꝓui'.

rows.opus_note: The texts are nearly identical, but X misreads 'weitläuftiger' as 'weitläufriger'; the other differences are only in how the brace layout is rendered.
rows.gemini_note: X transcribes the sulfur symbol '🜍' as earth '♁' ('△ oder ♁, das ewige Feuer') and misplaces the table brackets.

rows.opus_note: Y drops words from the Latin ('verba o-' becomes 'verationemque', 'qui solem ipsum' becomes 'quibus ipsum'), misreads 'eum concentum' as 'cum concentu', and garbles more of the Greek (e.g. 'δὲ' for 'γὰρ').
rows.gemini_note: Y corrupts the Latin by dropping 'solem' ('quibus ipsum' for 'qui solem ipsum') and severely garbles the Greek (e.g., 'τε ταμίας ὠσῆς' for 'τεταμένης πίσσης').

rows.opus_note: X adds a <margin> block taken from the facing leaf's text ('buf magnifid … c amerita') and misreads words such as 'fatam' for 'scitam', 'probidendiq' for 'prohibendiq', 'Cocitem' for 'Coclitem' and 'potem interfandi' for 'pontem interscindi'.
rows.gemini_note: X transcribes text from another leaf in a margin tag and introduces severe errors including 'interfandi' for 'interscindi' and 'alta tuſſa' for 'alia iuſſa'.

rows.opus_note: Y follows the print ('beweget', 'vñ ist die Straßburgische', 'erschiene', 'verdrucken'), while X normalizes u/v, drops 'vñ', and reads 'bewogen', 'erschienen' and 'verzucken'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'verdrucken' as 'verzucken' and omits 'vñ' before 'ist die Straßburgische Edition'.

rows.opus_note: The two texts are the same apart from the page number, which is printed '111' as Y has it, not 'III' as in X.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads the page number 'III' as '111'.

rows.opus_note: Y keeps the printed 'beßtem', 'gereichenden', 'gebracht/' and 'Getruckt zu Jtzstein', while X changes them to 'bestem', 'reichenden' and 'Gedruckt zu Idstein'.
rows.gemini_note: Y correctly transcribes 'gereichenden' and 'Getruckt zu Jtzstein', whereas X drops the prefix in 'reichenden' and modernizes the imprint to 'Gedruckt zu Idstein'.

rows.opus_note: Y keeps the printed 'Wurtzel'/'Holtz' and the catchword 'ser', while X modernizes them to 'Wurzel'/'Holz'; the wording is otherwise the same.
rows.gemini_note: Y faithfully preserves the printed spellings 'Wurtzel' and 'Holtz', whereas X modernizes them to 'Wurzel' and 'Holz'.

rows.opus_note: Y drops the 'XV.' heading and has OCR errors ('Aergten', 'Engenschafft', 'Arstneykunst', 'Schrifftimeister', and 'dieselbe rege' for 'dieselb erregt'), while X matches the print.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'Aertzten' as 'Aergten', 'dieselb erregt habe' as 'dieselbe rege habe', and 'Eygenschafft' as 'Engenschafft'.

rows.opus_note: X repeats the line '目成而後識之其與幾何萬', reads '物既號' where the leaf has '物段號' with a '數' gloss, and invents seal readings ('內閣文庫', '浅野家蔵'); Y is closer to the leaf ('天工開物巻序', '段', '免' glossed '既').
rows.gemini_note: X invents a duplicate final line ('目ノ成ル而後識ル之ヲ其與幾何ノ萬') and normalizes the manuscript's actual written characters ('段', '免', '築').

rows.opus_note: X is closer to the print ('baptizati', 'rursum crucifigentes', 'strennue'), while Y has 'baptizanti', 'rursus crucifigentes' and 'strenu-nue'; the wording is otherwise the same.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'baptizati' as 'baptizanti' and invents the reading 'mutila' where the leaf ends with hyphenated 'muti-'.

rows.opus_note: Y reads the print correctly ('Seque … Iecit … cadere', 'Concinitur'), while X has 'Sequitur', 'Ieit', 'Concinatur' and the sense-changing 'caedere' for 'cadere'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'Seque' as 'Sequitur', 'Iecit' as 'Ieit', and 'cadere' as 'caedere'.

rows.opus_note: In §11, X drops the clause 'hic uerò circulus aut est circulus sectionis, aut equidistans ei' and repeats '…transit per centrū residui glacialis. Et cum' in its place.
rows.gemini_note: X omits 'hic uerò circulus aut est circulus sectionis, aut equidistans ei' in proposition 11 and duplicates surrounding text.
